web.title: HSC results date revised to October 31
web.description:
The results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published on October 31, two days later than the date announced earlier.
Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, chairman of the Dhaka Education Board and head of the Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee, confirmed the revised date to The Daily Star today.
Education ministry and board sources said the change came amid complications over obtaining the prime minister’s consent to publish the results.
However, Prof Akhtaruzzaman dismissed the speculation, telling this newspaper that the new date had been finalised after consultation with the education minister.
The results were initially scheduled to be published on October 29.
On October 24, the committee issued a notice, signed by Akhtaruzzaman, announcing that date. The notice also said a press release detailing the arrangements would be issued on October 26.
However, no such press release was issued yesterday.
This year’s HSC and equivalent examinations began on July 2, with 12,70,583 candidates registered under 11 education boards.
Written examinations under most boards ended on August 8.

web.title: Bangladesh delegation, Kunming Medical University discuss expanding education ties
web.description:
A delegation from Bangladesh’s education ministry held talks with Kunming Medical University in China today on expanding cooperation in medical education, student training and joint research.
The delegation was led by Md Abdul Khaleque, senior secretary of the Secondary and Higher Education Division, according to a press release.
During a meeting at the university’s School of International Education, the two sides discussed student admissions, medical training, academic exchanges, joint research and long-term cooperation in medical education.
The Bangladeshi delegation expressed interest in strengthening ties with the university and creating opportunities for more Bangladeshi students to pursue medical education in China, the release said.
GM Farhan Isteaq, personal secretary to the education minister, accompanied the delegation.
Liu Yajie, dean of the School of International Education, briefed the visitors on the university’s international education and China study programmes, while Zhu Youbao, deputy secretary of the school, outlined admission policies and procedures for international students.
Bangladeshi students studying at the university also shared their academic and campus experiences.

The delegation also toured the campus and university museum.
In March last year, the First Affiliated Hospital of Kunming Medical University was among four hospitals in Yunnan province designated to treat Bangladeshi patients.

web.title: A digital trail to track learning gaps
web.description:
The government is planning a digital platform to store assessment records of students from classes 1 to 12, helping teachers track their progress and identify learning gaps.
Under the proposed “Unified Assessment System” (UAS), each student will receive a unique identification number, or Edu-ID, linked to their records across grades to create a “learning trajectory”, according to officials.
The platform will not determine how students are assessed or graded. Instead, teachers will enter assessment data into the system, which will generate progress reports and tabulation sheets.
A revised proposal for the Tk 124 crore project was recently sent to the Planning Commission for evaluation, according to a document from the Secondary and Higher Education Division.
Prof Khan Moinuddin Al Mahmud Sohel, acting director general of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE), told this newspaper that the commission is yet to discuss the proposal and might suggest changes.
Shefatul Islam, research officer at DSHE’s Research and Innovation Section, said student records are largely maintained by individual institutions, making it difficult to track progress across grades.
For instance, a student scoring 70 in math may perform well in algebra but struggle with geometry. Records maintained over several years could help identify such weaknesses, he said.
Shefatul said the National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB) will continue to design assessment methods, with UAS adapting to any changes.

The platform could eventually be expanded to include madrasa and technical education, he also said.
UAS is part of the proposed Tk 3,397 crore NextGen Secondary Education Programme, scheduled for January 2027 to December 2031. The programme also includes teacher training, digital classrooms and artificial intelligence laboratories.
Shefatul said funding for UAS could come from the Global Partnership for Education, a multi-stakeholder partnership hosted by the World Bank.
QUESTIONS OVER EFFECTIVENESS
Samir Ranjan Nath, programme head at the BRAC Institute of Educational Development at BRAC University, said, “The platform will undoubtedly generate a large dataset. However, the meaning of the data is a major question, as our school system lacks common assessment standards.”

web.title: HSC 2026 results on October 31: How to check your results online and via SMS
web.description:
The results of this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published on Saturday (October 31), with students able to check their results online, via SMS and through their educational institutions.
According to a notice issued by the Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee, the results will be announced at a programme beginning at 11:00am at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka.
The notice, signed by committee president Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, also chairman of the Dhaka Education Board, said students would be able to access their results through the available channels following the formal announcement.
**How to check results online**
Students can visit eduboardresults.gov.bd or educationboardresults.gov.bd, or the websites of their respective education boards.
They will need to select the examination, education board and examination year (2026), then enter their roll and registration numbers and other required details to view their results.
Educational institutions can download result sheets through the “Result” section of the websites by selecting their board and entering their Educational Institution Identification Number (EIIN). Students can also collect their results directly from their institutions.
**How to check results via SMS**
Students can check their results by sending an SMS to 16140 from a mobile phone.
They need to type HSC, followed by the first three letters of their education board's name, roll number and examination year, separated by spaces.
For example, a Dhaka Board candidate should type: HSC Dha 123456 2026
The message should then be sent to 16140.
**Re-evaluation applications**
Students wishing to have their results re-evaluated can apply online from November 1 to 7. Details of the application process will be available on the respective education boards’ websites.
A total of 12,70,583 candidates registered for this year's HSC and equivalent examinations under 11 education boards.
The results were initially scheduled to be published on October 29 but were later deferred to October 31.

web.title: HSC, equivalent exam results deferred to 31 Oct
web.description:
**The results of the 2026 Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published next Saturday (31 October), two days later than the previously announced date of 29 October.**
Professor Syed Akhtaruzzaman, president of the Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee and chairman of the Dhaka Education Board, confirmed the revised schedule to The Business Standard this afternoon (27 October).
The results will be formally announced at an event at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka on Saturday, he said.
Earlier, on 24 October, the coordination committee announced that the results would be published on 29 October. A notice signed by Akhtaruzzaman said details regarding the publication would be announced on 26 October.
The examinations began on 2 July this year. A total of 12,70,583 candidates registered for the examinations under 11 education boards.
Written examinations under most boards ended on 8 August. However, flooding delayed several examinations under the Chattogram Education Board, with the postponed written tests continuing until 9 September.
The examinations covered HSC under nine general education boards, Alim under the Madrasah Education Board, and HSC vocational and other equivalent programmes under the relevant boards.
